item.title: Midterm melee: Americans in the Netherlands gear up to vote
item.description:
Midterm melee: Americans in the Netherlands gear up to vote

October 18, 2026 Brandon Hartley

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Americans living abroad can often feel like they’re stuck on the political sidelines of their native land. With one of the most contentious midterm elections in US history coming up next month, we spoke with the Netherlands’ American community about how they’re getting involved in the race and the challenges they face.

For the past two years, Donald Trump has dominated headlines around the world. It seems like there’s little the divisive president and his administration haven’t disrupted within and well beyond US borders.

There’s no denying that much is riding on the country’s midterms on November 3 and that the result will have a defining impact on the course of global politics over the next few years.

As with prior elections, Americans living in the Netherlands may feel there’s little they can do besides mail in their absentee ballots – and even that is an often complicated process that many fail to complete.

Each state sets its own deadlines and decides whether ballots can go back by email, fax or post. A ballot posted from the Netherlands also has to cross the Atlantic in time to be counted.

Some don’t bother at all, and some feel they shouldn’t. “One of the reasons why many in the Netherlands don’t vote is because they’ve been here for a very long time,” said Tre’ Shawn Griffin-Noordermeer, vice chair of the Netherlands chapter of Democrats Abroad. “They feel like they shouldn’t be voting because they’ve lived outside the US for so long.”

In fact, federal law lets US citizens abroad keep voting in federal elections in the state where they last lived, however long they have been away.

To help get that message out, various groups here have been volunteering and hosting events in the days leading up to the midterms.

Reaching out to voters
Members of campaign group Democrats Abroad in the Netherlands have spent recent weeks running an email campaign and arranging “Vote From Abroad” gatherings on Zoom.

They’ve also been hosting lunches and other events in cities around the country to discuss the midterms along with putting up fliers and getting the word out on social media and via phone banking.

“We’ve got hundreds of volunteers here in the Netherlands who have been helping with this,” Griffin-Noordermeer told Dutch News. “A few weekends ago, we called over 13,000 people.”

Originally founded in 1964, Democrats Abroad serves as the Democratic party’s official organisation for American citizens living overseas. One of its primary tasks is encouraging its members and other voters, who are spread across 197 countries, to cast their ballots.

And that’s more difficult than it might seem.

Counting the voters
Nobody knows exactly how many Americans in the Netherlands can vote. The US does not require citizens to register with the government when they move abroad, and some states drop overseas voters from their rolls when they stop responding to election mail. That leaves neither the State Department nor voter lists with a reliable count.

The national statistics office CBS puts the number of US nationals living in the Netherlands at just over 27,000 in 2026 – though not all are old enough to vote, and Dutch-Americans with both passports are counted as Dutch, so aren’t included.

Worldwide, about 2.2 million Americans of voting age live abroad, according to the Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP), the US defence department office that helps military and overseas citizens vote. FVAP estimates only about 11% of them voted in the 2024 presidential election. Even fewer typically take part in midterms.

FVAP says 14.8% of eligible voters in Europe voted in 2024.

Preparing for the worst
Despite Trump’s low approval ratings, the path to a “blue wave” for the Democrats won’t necessarily be an easy one.

His administration also continues to meddle with the midterms. In August, the Pentagon, which runs FVAP, made last-minute changes to the Federal Post Card Application (the form overseas voters use to register and request ballots), removing the checkbox for US citizens who were born abroad and have never lived in the US. The Democratic National Committee has gone to court over the change.

That followed a March 2025 executive order in which Trump sought to add proof-of-citizenship requirements to the same form, parts of which federal courts have blocked. The order also aimed to stop states counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day.

In June, the US Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states can keep counting ballots postmarked by Election Day that arrive later. That matters for voters whose ballots travel by international post.

Hayley Hughes, the co-founder of the Netherlands chapter of Indivisible, admitted she’s worried about how things might go.

She has already had discussions with the leads of other chapters about what to do if the administration interferes with ballot counts or sends government agents to polling stations.

Trump has said Republicans should “take over the voting” in at least 15 places, and his former adviser Steve Bannon has welcomed the idea of immigration agents at the polls.

“We’re already thinking we might have to mobilise,” Hughes told Dutch News.

“We’re looking at a protest here that week, if needed. In the US, there could be a mass mobilisation of peaceful protests and a general strike where people don’t go to work or school. We all hope that won’t be needed.”

The week of the midterms

Several midterm events are scheduled for the week of the elections. The Atlantische Commissie in The Hague is hosting an “American midterm election breakfast” on 4 November.

In Amsterdam, the commission is also helping with the John Adams Institute’s “Midterm Madness” event on November 6. It’s set to serve as an afterparty with a ‘festival-style experience’ featuring live music along with discussions and lectures about the results featuring Mark Leibovich, a staff writer at The Atlantic, and others.

Comedian Greg Shapiro is once again teaming up with Pep Rosenfeld for an Election Night Party at Boom Chicago. They’ve hosted these events since the ‘00s and are once again prepared to stay up late. The comedy club has vowed to remain open past 4:00 “if things get crazy.”

“How late, well, we’ll wait and see,” Shapiro told Dutch News. “I’ve got performances the next day. At some point I’ll have to get some sleep.”

Shapiro will be taking a break from his ongoing ‘KING ME: 250 Years of Donald Trump’ comedy tour for the Boom Chicago gathering. He’s worried about how much rewriting he’ll have to do for subsequent performances after the midterms.

“There’s no telling what could happen,” he said. “It could become January 6th on a national scale.”

If you’re an American living overseas and haven’t voted yet, there could still be time based on where you’re registered. Visit votefromabroad.org for further assistance.

item.title: US ambassador to the NL gave $1m to Trump ballroom
item.description:
US ambassador to the NL gave $1m to Trump ballroom

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The US ambassador to the Netherlands, Joe Popolo, donated $1 million towards president Donald Trump’s new White House ballroom, according to a leaked list of project donors.

The Washington Post, which obtained the list, said the gift was made late last year, around two months after the businessman was appointed ambassador. Popolo declined to comment further to the paper.

The list runs to the end of September and records 67 donations of $10,000 or more, with a total of $333 million pledged. Tech, AI and arms manufacturers made up a large share of the donors. Some, who asked to stay anonymous, accounted for $77 million.

According to the paper, about half of the money came from companies or individuals with business before the federal government. Democratic politicians had previously asked for the donor list without success.

The fund managing the money agreed with the government not to reveal the identities of its backers, which US non-profits are generally not required to do.

Trump said last year the ballroom would be paid for entirely by himself and a few friends, but the list shows no contribution from the president. The Washington Post reported earlier this year that half the construction costs, now estimated at $600 million, are being met from public funds.

The White House snubbed the criticism, saying the same critics would complain if taxpayers were paying for the renovations.

The ballroom, which the president says will hold nearly 1,000 guests, is being built on the site of the White House east wing, which Trump had demolished last year. The plans include a military bunker underneath.

item.title: Limburg named the world’s “most intelligent region”
item.description:
Limburg named the world’s “most intelligent region”

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Limburg has been named the world’s smartest region by the US-based think tank Intelligent Community Forum (ICF). The southern province, known for its hills and regional dialects, beat finalists from countries like Taiwan and Canada.

The award was presented to Brightlands, a network of four business and research campuses in the province that focus on health, AI, sustainable chemistry and food research. The ICF, a federation of 200 cities and regions, ranks areas around the globe each year on factors like economic and social development.

The jury praised the cooperation between government, business and research institutions at the campuses, as well as the way Limburg rebuilt itself after its coal mines closed half a century ago. After natural gas was discovered in 1959, “the region lost not only jobs but also security and hope,” ICF founder Robert Bell said.

Brightlands was set up in 2014 by the provincial government, education institutions and local businesses, according to L1 Nieuws.

The Maastricht campus focuses on health and is linked to the university hospital, while Heerlen, home to pension fund ABP and the national statistics office CBS, specialises in data and AI.

The materials campus is on the Chemelot chemical site in Sittard-Geleen, and Venlo’s food campus uses infrastructure left over from the 2012 Floriade horticultural expo.

Limburg beat six other finalists, from Brazil, Turkey, the US, Canada, Spain and Taiwan. Last year’s winner was Durham Region in Canada. The Brainport region around Eindhoven won in 2011.

item.title: Self-employment declines as freelancers quickly find new jobs
item.description:
Self-employment declines as freelancers quickly find new jobs

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

After two decades of mostly uninterrupted growth, self-employment in the Netherlands has declined this year for the first time, with former freelancers quickly finding new jobs, according to the Dutch central bank (DNB).

There are 10% fewer self-employed workers this year than in 2024. Their numbers have fallen by some 131,000 since the end of 2024, when they peaked at almost 1.3 million.

In mid-2026, around 12% of the workforce was primarily self-employed, still a substantial share by international standards.

Little impact on unemployment
But according to the DNB, the decline has had little impact on unemployment, with half of former freelancers finding paid work within three months. About a third move to permanent positions or to jobs with prospects of a permanent contract. Others move into flex work. Only 7% become unemployed, which is comparable to previous years.

“Leaving self-employment therefore mainly results in movement within the labour market rather than a greater flow into unemployment,” the DNB said.

About half of former self-employed workers move to different sectors entirely, especially healthcare and social care, education and government, retail, transport and hospitality.

The DNB says this confirms that the Dutch labour market is dynamic. However, its research does not show how people’s income, productivity or employment conditions change after they leave self-employment for new work.

The DNB says it cannot say definitively why the decrease is happening. It does note that stricter enforcement against so-called false self-employment since 2025 may play a role.

“We observe relatively high levels of movement between self-employment and employment in sectors where false self-employment is frequently debated, including healthcare, construction, facility services and business services,” it said.

item.title: Former parliamentarian targeted for banned Israeli wine purchase
item.description:
Former parliamentarian targeted for banned Israeli wine purchase

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A complaint has been filed against former orthodox Protestant SGP MP Roelof Bisschop, who said publicly that he had bought wine in protest against the Dutch ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements, public broadcaster NOS reported.

Pro-Palestinian group BDS Netherlands (Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions) filed the criminal complaint with the public prosecution service (OM). Activists had earlier reported Bisschop to the fiscal investigation service FIOD.

Bisschop bought two bottles on September 23, the day after the ban took effect, and posted a photo of them on social media. Two days later he told Christian television channel Family7 that the purchase was a “statement” against the ban.

Since September 22, the Netherlands has banned imports of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories and the Golan Heights. The rules also ban buying and selling such goods, intermediary trade and any form of circumvention.

In its complaint, BDS Netherlands said Bisschop had deliberately acted against the sanctions policy and promoted this on several platforms.

“Anyone who, as a former MP, publicly announces they are deliberately testing the law can expect the OM to look at whether that is a criminal offence,” the group said in the complaint.

It is not yet clear whether the wine is covered by the ban. The producer, Teperberg Winery, has vineyards in the occupied West Bank and is on a UN list of companies active in settlements. However, it says these wines are made just inside Israel. Bisschop told NOS he did not know exactly where the bottles came from.

The OM said it is aware of the complaint and will assess whether there are grounds to open an investigation.

item.title: Dutch wartime biography pulled from shelves over falsehoods
item.description:
Dutch wartime biography pulled from shelves over falsehoods

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The biography of 99-year-old Dutchman Willem Wilbrink, Getekend voor het leven in Dachau en Indië (Marked for Life in Dachau and the Dutch East Indies), has been taken off bookshelves and online platforms at the publisher’s request after researchers found his claims of being a resistance hero and Dachau survivor were likely untrue.

The 2023 biography by author Laurens van Aggelen recounts Wilbrink’s claims that he was imprisoned in the Dachau concentration camp at the age of 16, where he allegedly saved 40 people’s lives. He claimed he took people who had been sent to the incineration ovens but were still alive to the infirmary.

But an investigation published in the history magazine Historisch Nieuwsblad earlier this month by Hans Vogelzang, whose wife’s father was imprisoned in Dachau, found no supporting evidence for Wilbrink’s claims in either camp memoirs or archives. He wasn’t even listed in the camp’s complete prisoner list, which is said to be extremely accurate.

Wilbrink is a well-known figure, a regular at Second World War commemorations where he wears medals that have also come under suspicion, including a Polish “hero title”. Several Dachau survivors have no memory of the stories he told.

Lingering doubts

According to GLD news, the Dachau Committee has doubted Wilbrink’s war story since 2024. “We have been closely involved in the article for several weeks,” said Wimar Jaeger, mayor of Zutphen and chairman of the Dutch Dachau Committee. “It’s not a surprise. The biography of Wilbrink that came out… raised a lot of questions for us. We couldn’t believe what was in there. It was almost impossible.”

At the time, the committee tried to get the publisher to withdraw the book. “We’re not out for a publicity wave that harms a 99-year-old man,” Jaeger told GLD. “He is a vulnerable elderly gentleman whose war trauma may have left him with images in his head that are not in line with reality. As a committee, we know what war trauma can do to memories and we are empathetic and understanding about it.”

But as the falsehoods continued to be presented as facts, the committee took more public action. “Then we have no choice but to make clear in this way that it’s not right. Facts and reality must be safeguarded, because if they turn out not to be correct, you no longer have a cautionary tale. That is especially important at a time like this, which in various respects resembles the run-up to the Second World War.”

Author Van Aggelen has rejected the criticism and says he stands by his biography, while Wilbrink himself has called the Historisch Nieuwsblad article “slander and libel” and maintains Dachau’s records were incomplete. The publisher, White Elephant Media in Arnhem, has yet to comment.

item.title: Police quietly seize left-wing activist server for US government
item.description:
Police quietly seize left-wing activist server for US government

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amsterdam police have seized a server belonging to Autistici/Inventati (A/I), a dissolved hacker network that provided online services and support to left-wing political groups. The US says this included Antifa, which the Trump administration has designated a terror organisation.

The server, located at the Science Park in the east of the city, was taken without any public announcement by local police. A spokesperson told NRC that an image of the server would go “straight to America”.

Trade association Dutch Cloud Community has demanded clarity over why the police agreed to the US’ demand. The public prosecution department has also made no official statement about the incident.

Politicians have also expressed dismay over the seizure. MP Barbara Kathmann, of opposition party PRO, told the Volkskrant it “sets a dangerous precedent”.

In September, after A/I shut down its services, Kathmann and D66 MP Sarah El Boujdaini warned in a letter to parliament that the US could paralyse European internet providers for political purposes.

Similar fears have arisen over the potential acquisition of Solvinity, the cloud provider that hosts Dutch government services like DigiD, by an American company.

item.title: ABN Amro caught in crossfire amid ICC sanctions
item.description:
ABN Amro caught in crossfire amid ICC sanctions

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch bank ABN Amro, which handles the finances of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, could face heavy US penalties if it keeps doing so once American sanctions take effect next April, RTL has reported.

The US government announced sanctions against the ICC last week, a significant escalation after it had already sanctioned 13 of the court’s judges and officials. The US says the court threatens American service personnel, and has attacked its decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant.

The sanctions will freeze any ICC assets in the US and bar Americans from providing funds, goods or services to the court. The measures have been delayed for 180 days to allow time for diplomatic talks, and are due to take full effect on April 7, 2027.

ABN Amro is exposed through ABN Amro Clearing, the division that settles share trades for clients and has a large US business. RTL reported that this gives Washington the leverage to fine the bank, bring criminal charges or, in the worst case, put ABN Amro itself on the sanctions list.

The Financieele Dagblad reported that the clearing division made a net profit of €298 million in 2025. The Dutch state is ABN Amro’s largest shareholder.

It is not clear how real the risk is. “The legislation is not at all clearly worded,” Cedric Ryngaert, professor of international public law at Utrecht University, told RTL. He said the uncertainty creates a “chilling effect”, because companies cannot tell whether they are covered.

The cabinet has condemned the sanctions. Prime minister Rob Jetten called them “deeply regrettable” but said dialogue with Washington was still important.

Legal experts and campaign groups want the European Commission to activate the EU’s blocking statute, which would bar European companies from complying with the US measures.

The cabinet previously told MPs it would push for activation if new sanctions were expected to seriously hamper the court’s work.

If that happened, ABN Amro could be forced to choose between breaking EU rules and breaking US ones, RTL said.

item.title: Suspected arson in Amsterdam evacuates 55 homes, man arrested
item.description:
Suspected arson in Amsterdam evacuates 55 homes, man arrested

October 16, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A 26-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of arson after a fire broke out in an underground parking garage overnight Friday.

The parking garage is located on Theodoor van Hoytemastraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, where some 55 homes above it had to be evacuated.

The local safety authority, which coordinates emergency services, said the building sustained significant damage and that the apartments are currently uninhabitable. Power to the area has also temporarily been shut off.

Police are looking into the possibility that the incident stemmed from a personal conflict. The suspect was arrested early Friday morning.

One person at the scene went to hospital of their own accord, but no other injuries were reported. Five cars caught fire in the blaze, and the car park sustained heavy smoke and structural damage.

Residents were put up in a nearby hotel. As of Friday morning, they were still unable to return home pending a damage assessment. Authorities say the building’s electrical and sewage systems were also damaged.

Some surrounding homes and businesses have also been left without electricity.

Police are asking anyone who may have witnessed the incident between 2-3am to contact the investigation tip line at 0800-6070.
